articles.title: Ship captains and crews transiting the Strait of Hormuz make so much danger pay that they’re ‘almost being viewed as mercenaries’
articles.summary: Tanker captains can earn $100,000 a month for transiting the strait, plus a $50,000 bonus for each trip, and sailors can make at least four to six times thei...
articles.body:
The high-risk, high-reward business of moving oil through the Strait of Hormuz has gotten riskier and more rewarding.

Despite steady attacks from Iran, oil tankers and other commercial vessels have continued flowing through the narrow waterway. With protection from the U.S. military and help from pipelines bypassing the strait, Persian Gulf oil flows returned to prewar levels .

But seeking to reassert its leverage over the global oil chokepoint, Iran has stepped up drone and missile strikes on ships recently, including those outside the immediate vicinity of Hormuz.

While traffic has dipped in response, ships continue to cross, with many making shuttle runs in and out of the Gulf to unload oil cargoes via ship-to-ship transfers. Then other vessels deliver the barrels to customers.

For those onboard the ships willing to tolerate the risks in the Gulf, a hefty payday awaits. Tanker captains can earn $100,000 a month for transiting the strait, plus a $50,000 bonus for each trip, sources told the Financial Times .

That "danger money" is up from regular pay of about $15,000 a month and is necessary for shipowners to keep their fleets crewed.

Meanwhile, sailors typically make at little as $1,500 a month. But trips through Hormuz can bump up earnings by at least four to six times their normal rates, the report said.

Other hotspots also offer hazard enhancements, albeit less than what's available for Hormuz trips. According to the FT , captains and sailors get double pay in the southern Red Sea, where Houthis have been attacking Saudi ships, and in the Gulf of Oman, where many ship-to-ship transfers take place after Hormuz shuttle runs.

Because many ships and their crews are dedicated to the shuttle runs, they are in constant peril—allowing them to stack up all the bonuses and danger money for each trip.

A source told the FT that those brave enough to stomach the nearly constant threat of attacks are "almost being viewed as mercenaries," though some unwilling crew members are reportedly being pressured to stay onboard.

Since the Iran war started on Feb. 28, at least 93 ships have been hit, and 24 sailors have been killed, according to the International Maritime Organization.

In addition to the hazard pay for crews, shipowners are also paying for insurance, and the war risk can command 6% to 10% of a ship's value—translating to up to $20 million for a supertanker sailing through the Gulf.

All the added costs have made shipping expensive too. Freight rates for cargoes crossing the Strait of Hormuz hit a record high of $1.3 million per day, up from last year's daily rate of $20,000 to $50,000.

articles.title: Jeff Bezos says he gets why socialism is surging—but politicians blaming ‘greedy landlords’ have housing all wrong
articles.summary: A record 43% of Americans now view socialism favorably. The Amazon founder blames government policy for the housing crunch and holds up Austin, where rents h...
articles.body:
Jeff Bezos says he understands why socialism is gaining traction in America. The affordability crisis is real, especially when it comes to housing. But the Amazon and Blue Origin founder argues that some politicians are blaming the wrong culprit.

In an interview with Fox News' Bret Baier that aired Wednesday on Special Report , Bezos said government intervention has often been counterproductive in housing, while some politicians point fingers at "greedy landlords" instead of addressing what he called a basic supply-and-demand problem. "It's econ 101," he said. In the same interview, Bezos predicted AI could usher in a three-day workweek , as Fortune reported. He has also argued that raising taxes on billionaires won't fix affordability .

Americans are growing more receptive to socialism, as their views of Big Business sour.

Capitalism still has broader appeal, with 55% of Americans viewing it positively, according to a Gallup poll released in September . But a record 43% now view socialism positively, the highest share since Gallup began tracking the question in 2010. Meanwhile, positive views of Big Business have fallen from 49% in 2010 to just 35%.

The generational divide is stark. Among Americans ages 18 to 34, 57% view socialism positively, compared with 43% who view capitalism favorably. For Americans 55 and older, the picture is reversed: 65% view capitalism positively, versus 34% for socialism.

In a separate Gallup survey , 26% of Americans cited a stronger safety net and more affordable essentials, including housing, health care, and education, as benefits of socialism. Still, 45% either said nothing was good about socialism or couldn't name any of its benefits.

Even Vice President JD Vance warned in July that young Americans priced out of homeownership could be drawn to socialism, as Fortune previously reported .

At the end of 2025, a household needed $120,800 a year to afford payments on a median-price U.S. home, up from $68,700 five years earlier, according to Harvard University's Joint Center for Housing Studies . Only 32% of U.S. households met that income threshold, including just 16% of renter households.

An earlier report from the same Harvard center found that rising homebuying costs between 2021 and 2024 effectively priced out about 8 million renter households that previously earned enough to afford a median-price home. Most were between age 25 and 44, in their prime homebuying years. First-time buyers made up just 21% of home purchases in the National Association of Realtors' latest annual survey , a record low, and Zillow's CEO doesn't expect that to change soon .

articles.title: SpaceX stock poised for a catalyst-fueled 2027
articles.summary: 2027 will be eventful for SpaceX.
articles.body:
SpaceX ( SPCX ) isn't going quietly into what could be an eventful 2027.

Elon Musk's rocket business said late last week it acquired a nationwide low-band spectrum portfolio . It positions Musk's satellite business, Starlink, to challenge legacy wireless giants across the US.

Shares of AT&T ( T ), T-Mobile ( TMUS ), and Verizon ( VZ ) tanked on the news on Friday.

Meanwhile, SpaceX is reportedly seeking to raise $40 billion in financing to purchase Nvidia chips.

"The debate is whether a company this early in its public life should carry that much leverage," Yorkville Ives partner Dan Ives said. "We think the contracted backlog in AI and the cash generation of Starlink give SpaceX the capacity to service it, and we would rather see this compute financed and deployed than deferred."

With the year winding down, here is a helpful calendar of potential catalysts for SpaceX in 2027 to tuck away for later. It's important to be overprepared as an investor, especially on a news-driven stock like SpaceX.

Of everything on the calendar, we would circle June 12, 2027 (and the weeks leading up to it). Elon Musk agreed not to sell any of his roughly 40% to 46.1% equity stake — more than 6 billion shares — for 366 calendar days following SpaceX's IPO on June 12, 2026.

Investors will carefully watch whether Musk sells SpaceX stock after the lockup. For one, a large supply of stock in the market from Musk could weigh on the share price. And two, the mere sign of Musk selling may unsettle the SpaceX believers.

articles.title: US mortgage bond funds suffer one of worst outflows since 2021
articles.summary: Investors fled US mortgage bond funds at historic levels over the past three weeks, with outflows ranking among the seven worst since the start of 2021, as s...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Investors fled US mortgage bond funds at historic levels over the past three weeks, with outflows ranking among the seven worst since the start of 2021, as surging interest rates spur a flight from volatility.

The Bloomberg US Mortgage Backed Securities Index marked its second worst performance on record in September. The selling follows a spike in Treasury yields to multi-decade highs, fueled by surging oil prices, inflation concerns, and expectations of Federal Reserve interest rate hikes.

Mortgage-backed securities are highly sensitive to sudden fluctuations in bond yields, which serve as the benchmarks for borrowing costs throughout the economy. When interest rates rise, homeowners tend to stop refinancing their home loans, keeping investors locked into lower-yielding securities for longer than they may had previously expected.

"Fed policy tightening and a flatter curve may reduce demand from banks, a key source of MBS demand," Erica Adelberg, senior MBS strategist at Bloomberg Intelligence, wrote. "On the positive side, MBS supply should trend lower into year-end, with the highest mortgage rates since 2023 reducing refinancing and home-purchase demand and potentially slowing home-price and loan-size appreciation."

The Treasuries selloff in September sent yields on long-dated bonds to 24-year highs. Coupled with the underperformance in mortgage-backed securities on an excess return basis, the MBS index logged the second-most negative year-to-date total return in its 50-year history, Adelberg said.

articles.title: Amid surge in power generation, volume of natural gas traded on IGX platform triples YoY
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The volume of natural gas traded on Indian Gas Exchange (IGX) more than tripled year-on-year in Sept to a record 17.8 trillion British thermal
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The volume of natural gas traded on Indian Gas Exchange (IGX) more than tripled year-on-year in Sept to a record 17.8 trillion British thermal units (TBtu), with power generators accounting for a large share of the surge in free-market gas purchases.The traded volume was 40.6% higher than in Aug and surpassed the previous monthly record of 15.9 TBtu, recorded in April 2025.India’s power consumption in Sept rose 11.3% year-on-year to 162 billion units, driven by cooling and irrigation demand amid a monsoon deficit.IGX said power generators bought 10.4 TBtu of the 12.8 TBtu of free-market gas traded on the exchange during the month. The Sept purchase was more than twice the 4.5 TBtu bought by gas-based power plants through IGX during the entire April-May period. Peak power demand had reached an all-time high of 271 GW in May 2026, driven by intense summer cooling requirements.While the total installed capacity of gas-based power plants is 20.1 GW, only 11.2 GW was available in Sept. These plants generated 3,905 million units of electricity, 60% more than the 2,440 million units produced in the same month in 2025. Despite their small share in the overall generation mix, gas-based plants play a balancing role during evening peak hours, when solar output falls. This role has become more significant as hydropower generation has declined amid a rainfall deficit.“The traded volume during Sep’26 increased by 208.2% YoY and 40.6% MoM, primarily driven by higher demand from the power sector, which raised overall gas demand on the exchange,” said Rajesh Kumar Mediratta, MD & CEO, Indian Gas Exchange.Nearly 66% of the gas bought by the power sector in Sept was traded through balance-of-month contracts, while another 30.3% was traded through intraday and day-ahead contracts, IGX said.Gas prices also rose sharply during the month. IGX’s benchmark GIXI price increased 29% from Aug to Rs 2,712 per million British thermal units (MMBtu) in Sept, 161% higher than a year earlier.The strong performance in Sept took IGX’s traded volume in the first half of FY27 to a record 69.5 TBtu, up 70.8% from the year-earlier period. articles.title: Rs 5.89 crore FD interest slashed from 7.75% to 3.5% without notice; Delhi High Court rejects bank’s non-renewal argument and orders interest at an average of earlier rates
articles.summary: Can banks change the rate of returns for fixed deposits on non-renewal?
articles.body: Can banks change the rate of returns for fixed deposits on non-renewal? The Delhi High Court has ruled in favour of a fixed deposit holder after a bank cut the interest rate on his Rs 5.89-crore FD from 7.75% to 3.5%.In its September 23, 2026, ruling, the Delhi High Court directed the bank to pay the highest applicable interest rate on the deposit, granting relief to the FD holder.What the case is aboutThe fixed deposit had been opened after a court order which arose from a dispute between two parties. The parties had opted for arbitration to resolve the matter under Section 9 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996.Also Read | Man invested Rs 10 lakh, which tax department treated as unexplained; he first cited cash loan, then bank withdrawals as source, ITAT Nagpur deletes addition and Rs 2.11 lakh penaltyIn an order passed in 2008, the Delhi High Court directed that the Rs 5.89 crore held in the deposit holder's bank account be kept secured in a bank until the dispute was resolved by the court. It also instructed the bank to create a fixed deposit for the entire amount, carrying the maximum rate of interest.Initially, the FD earned interest at rates of 7.75%, 8.25% and 7.75% over different periods.However, from January 30, 2018, the bank lowered the rate to 3.5%. Challenging the reduction, the deposit holder approached the court again, arguing that the bank had cut the interest rate without any valid reason or justification.Representing the bank, its lawyer argued that Clause 3.3 of the RBI circular allowed the bank to decide the interest rate applicable to the fixed deposit. The lawyer also invoked Clause 3.4 of the circular, contending that if a fixed deposit receipt was not renewed upon maturity, the deposit would earn interest at the prevailing savings bank rate.'Also Read | Retired bank employee got Rs 12.27 lakh leave encashment and claimed Rs 3 lakh exemption in 2020, but government later hiked limit to Rs 25 lakh in 2023; ITAT Chennai allows full tax exemptionWhy did the fixed deposit holder win the case?The Delhi High Court observed that Clause 3.3 of the RBI circular gives banks the freedom to set interest rates on domestic term deposits across different tenures. However, this discretion comes with a condition: banks cannot discriminate between deposits accepted on the same date, whether they are held at the same branch or at different branches of the bank.The Delhi High Court noted that the interest rate on the FD in question, which had been created following an earlier court order, was reduced. However, the bank failed to establish that the interest rate on all comparable fixed deposits had also been brought down to 3.5%.The court also noted that the order did not specify the period for which the FD had to be maintained. However, there was no evidence to show that the bank had informed the affected parties, namely the deposit holder and the third party, that the deposit had matured and needed to be renewed.Nor had the bank approached the arbitrator or the High Court for directions on renewing the FD. It had also not informed either forum that the winding-down of its operations had prompted it to reduce the deposit's interest rate to the savings bank rate.Also Read | 83-year-old woman got Rs 12.28 lakh after son’s death, but sought Rs 15,000 maintenance from college-going granddaughter and a share of family pension from son’s widow; Kerala HC rejects both claimsBanks may reduce the interest paid on fixed deposits, but their actions must remain within the limits prescribed by the RBI and comply with its rules, Siddartha Karnani, Partner at King Stubb and Kasiva, told ET.Karnani explained that under the RBI's rules, when a term deposit or fixed deposit reaches maturity and the money is not paid out, the unclaimed amount earns interest at the savings account rate. This was also the basis of the bank's position in the Delhi High Court case, he said, referring to the relevant RBI circular.The rules, however, were amended in July 2021. Under the revised provision, an overdue deposit earns interest at either the savings account rate or the rate originally agreed upon, whichever is lower. The amended wording is set out in paragraph 10.2 of the RBI's Master Direction on Interest Rate on Deposits, 2025.Co-operative banks, however, operate under a separate set of directions. As a result, the specific provision applicable to a deposit depends on the type of bank involved.Despite having the discretion to set deposit rates, banks cannot apply them arbitrarily, Karnani said. Two fixed deposits accepted on the same date for the same tenure cannot be given different interest rates. Banks must also explain how they calculate interest when accepting deposits and display the relevant information at their branches.Also Read | Man paid Rs 1.73 crore for Gurgaon flat, waited over a decade without possession; builder alleges homebuyer bought it for commercial gain, consumer commission awards refund with 12% interest & Rs 4 lakhFurther, where a depositor has provided an explicit instruction to renew an FD automatically, the bank should follow that instruction instead of allowing the deposit to become overdue and earn interest at a lower rate.According to Siddartha Karnani, the bank's failure to treat the deposit differently from a regular customer FD, despite it being governed by a court order, was central to its defeat. It also failed to inform the parties that it had reduced the interest rate.The Single Judge's May 22, 2019 order had directed the bank to deposit the amount with the Registrar General, with interest from January 30, 2018 calculated using the average of the three earlier rates. The Division Bench upheld those directions and dismissed the bank’s appeal on September 23, 2026.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 3 charts sum up why many US households are struggling right now
articles.summary: Here are several charts from the Goldman Sachs team that shed light on the realities facing many US households, and why a lot of consumer companies are strug...
articles.body:
The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) trading near a record high doesn't mean all is fine and dandy in the US economy. Quite the contrary for many households as they battle higher costs for gas , fuel , and medical insurance this year.

Consumer sentiment fell to 46.3 in October, down 1.8 points from September's reading of 48.1, according to the latest from the University of Michigan. The result represented a five-month low.

Pressured household finances have appeared in the crop of third quarter earnings reports from packaged food companies. Food and beverage giant PepsiCo ( PEP ) slashed its full-year profit outlook last week . That came on the heels of spice-maker McCormick ( MKC ) reporting sluggish demand in its most recent quarter.

"We don't expect the consumer to suddenly become in a much better place in the next 12 to 18 months," PepsiCo CEO Ramon Laguarta said on the company's earnings call.

Here are several charts from the Goldman Sachs team that shed light on the realities facing many US households, and why a lot of consumer companies are struggling.

With the cost of living remaining high, households are taking on more debt to get by. Household debt now tops $18 trillion .

In addition to taking on more debt, households have dipped into their savings to spend on what they need to spend on. Personal savings rates are below the long-term average.

Inflation has eaten up worker wages. In September, average hourly earnings rose just 0.1% month over month and 3% year over year, according to Labor Department data. Government data found that, in August, inflation increased 3.4% year over year.

articles.title: Anthropic PBC admits India arm is subsidiary in Belagavi brand dispute
articles.summary: Anthropic PBC tells Belagavi court its Bengaluru unit, Anthropic India Pvt Ltd, is a subsidiary in “Anthropic” brand dispute; next hearing Nov 13.
articles.body: Belagavi: US-based AI company Anthropic PBC has told a Belagavi court that Bengaluru-based Anthropic India Pvt Ltd is its subsidiary, a disclosure that could influence an ongoing brand dispute with Belagavi-based Anthropic Softwares Pvt Ltd.The statement was filed before the 8th Additional District and Sessions Court, Belagavi, on Monday. The case, initiated in January 2026, concerns rights to the “Anthropic” brand name. Anthropic Softwares had alleged that Anthropic India projected itself as a separate legal entity with no connection to the US parent, forcing the plaintiff to serve summons on Anthropic PBC in the US. The process took nearly four months before the American company appeared before the court.In its latest written submission, Anthropic PBC acknowledged that Anthropic India Pvt Ltd is its subsidiary. The filing also referred to a meeting in Aug 2026 between a delegation led by Anthropic India managing director Irina Ghose and Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar. According to the statement, Karnataka govt had explored possibilities of enabling secure access to govt datasets for developing AI-powered public solutions while ensuring data sovereignty and residency requirements.During arguments, advocate MM Sheikh, representing the plaintiff, said the admission contradicted the earlier position that the Indian entity was independent of the US company. He alleged that the subsidiary’s earlier claims had prolonged the litigation and created procedural hurdles.Sheikh opposed Anthropic PBC’s challenge to the Belagavi court’s jurisdiction, arguing that a company with global operations could not selectively dispute jurisdiction where its activities had commercial implications. He further submitted that Anthropic Softwares Pvt Ltd, established in 2017, had built goodwill under the Anthropic brand in India and overseas before Anthropic PBC, founded in 2021, commenced its India operations in 2024.Judge RP Gowda adjourned the matter to Nov 13 for further proceedings.You use AI every day. articles.title: Government moves to set up mineral exchange, 5 commodities to be traded initially
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Government has moved a step closer to setting up the country’s first mineral exchange to facilitate transparent trading of bulk industrial
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Government has moved a step closer to setting up the country’s first mineral exchange to facilitate transparent trading of bulk industrial commodities, with the mines ministry initiating the process to select an entity to establish and operate the platform.The exchange aims at bringing greater transparency to mineral trading by ensuring a “fair, transparent, neutral, efficient and robust price discovery” mechanism. Officials said it would initially cover five minerals - iron ore, chromite, bauxite, limestone and manganese - and may later include other minerals - except coal, lignite and atomic minerals - with regulatory approval.These five minerals are crucial raw materials for heavy industries, particularly steelmaking, aluminium production and cement, and have established domestic mining and industrial supply chains. The mineral exchange is likely to become functional by the next financial year.“The exchange will operate through a centralised electronic platform and facilitate physical delivery-based contracts, providing a transparent and competitive mechanism for pricing and mineral supplies. It is expected to improve market access and reduce disputes over quality, pricing and contract terms,” an official said, adding that companies have been asked to submit applications for setting up the exchange.Currently, mineral sales take place through direct transactions between producers and consumers, as well as electronic auctions. India has separate exchanges for electricity and natural gas, while the process to set up the country’s first coal exchange is on.The ministry of mines has notified the rules, while the Indian Bureau of Mines has been appointed as the nodal agency and regulator.You use AI every day. articles.title: Abolish long-term capital gains tax for equity: SBI Research recommends, says ‘government must anchor hot money flows’
articles.summary: With foreign investors pulling money out of Indian equities, economists at the country's largest lender, State Bank of India (SBI), have proposed
articles.body: With foreign investors pulling money out of Indian equities, economists at the country's largest lender, State Bank of India (SBI), have proposed scrapping the long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax on equity investments to encourage investors to remain invested for longer periods."The government must seriously look into anchoring hot money flows into equity segment by extending the holding period to say 2-3 years and abolishing the long-term capital gains tax for equity," SBI Research said in its Ecowrap report.The proposal is aimed at making foreign capital flows into equities more stable and limiting the chances of abrupt withdrawals that could put pressure on the rupee.The report acknowledged the recent measures taken by RBI to curb pressure on the rupee.“The RBI has taken cudgels, firing a bazooka of measures to arrest the depreciating trends in rupee value,” it said.“While the RBI has been taking all possible steps to thwart a seemingly difficult global playbook, there is an urgent need also by the government to address some of the long pending structural issues regarding capital inflows,” the report said.Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) currently face a 12.5% LTCG tax on equity investments. The Union Budget 2026 retained this rate for listed shares and equity mutual funds, continuing the tax framework introduced as part of a major fiscal overhaul in 2024.Foreign investors have sold Indian equities worth Rs 44,166 crore so far in October. This has pushed their total withdrawals from the market to more than Rs 3 lakh crore in 2026. Investor sentiment has been affected by elevated crude oil prices, a stronger US dollar and rising US bond yields. At the same time, an artificial intelligence-driven rally in North Asian markets is drawing foreign capital towards the region.The latest selling has taken FPI outflows from Indian equities in 2026 to Rs 3.04 lakh crore, substantially exceeding the Rs 1.66 lakh crore withdrawn during the whole of 2025, according to the data cited in the report.Experts attribute the continued selling to several factors, including India's lack of stocks linked to the artificial intelligence theme and rising bond yields in other markets, particularly the US. These markets offer investors comparatively higher risk-free returns.SBI Research suggests changes to export proceeds and tax rulesThe report also recommended simplifying the process for repatriating export earnings, with a reasonable timeframe of around six months. SBI Research noted that exporters generally offer overseas buyers credit periods of a similar duration. Any request to extend the repatriation period beyond six months should be considered individually, it said.These proposals are intended to support foreign currency inflows and strengthen the stability of India's external accounts. SBI Research called for policy changes that encourage foreign investors to take longer-term positions and ensure that export proceeds are brought back within a reasonable period.The report also called for greater clarity on withholding tax applicable to external commercial borrowings (ECBs), which currently ranges from 5% to 20%.It said clearer rules were needed to ensure that borrowers receive the benefits available under Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements (DTAAs) and that tax authorities apply general and specific provisions consistently. articles.title: Aequs signs long-term aerospace deals with Safran
articles.summary: Aequs signs long-term Safran supply deals for Airbus A320/A330/A350 and Boeing 787 components, expanding work to Hosur AECE and six Safran units.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Aequs has signed long-term supply agreements with French aerospace major Safran for critical components used in Airbus and Boeing aircraft programmes, expanding a relationship spanning more than a decade and extending it to two additional Safran entities.The agreements cover machining of superalloy parts and the machining, coating and assembly of landing gear components for the Airbus A320, A330 and A350, and Boeing 787 programmes. A significant portion of the work will be undertaken at Aequs’ upcoming Engine Components Ecosystem (AECE) in Hosur in Tamil Nadu.The agreements build on Aequs’ existing relationship with Safran Landing Systems and extend the collaboration to Safran Aerosystems and Safran Electronics & Defense. Aequs now has relationships with six Safran entities, the company said.The company will use its integrated manufacturing capabilities across forging, precision machining, special processes, surface treatment and assembly to manufacture the components. Its Belagavi Aerospace Cluster will continue to serve as a manufacturing base for global aerospace supply chains, with the Hosur facility expanding its capacity for medium and large engine components.“These agreements reflect what Aequs was built for: long-horizon partnerships anchored in capability, reliability, and scale,” said Aravind Melligeri, executive chairman and CEO of Aequs. He said the components were among the more demanding flight-critical products to industrialise, and that the awards reflected the trust built with customers and the capabilities developed across its manufacturing ecosystems.The announcement follows an agreement signed by Aequs and Safran Landing Systems in July 2026 to supply fully assembled wheels for the Airbus A320 family. That contract, extending through 2042, marked Aequs’ first serial production agreement spanning more than 15 years. The wheels will be manufactured in India, from locally sourced aluminium to final assembly and testing.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: A wealth boom and a price shock are colliding ahead of the midterm elections
articles.summary: The historic technological revolution underway is creating investment gains among the already rich and leaving the rest of the population behind.
articles.body: The United States is in the middle of a historic and costly technological revolution, with the artificial intelligence buildout driving a level of investment set to eclipse the previous telecommunications boom, as well as national projects like the construction ​of rail and highway networks. The transformation has spurred immense stock market gains that have boosted household wealth across the economy, which arguably has helped to keep consumer spending on track. ‌But with investment gains concentrated among the already rich, some Americans are benefiting more than others. And what’s been dubbed a crisis of affordability can still be seen in the rising cost of homeownership or the price of ground beef — a meaningful pinch for the great majority of households that derive most of their income from earnings rather than investments. A bigger slice for the 1% Ninety-nine percent of U.S. households have cause to wonder what the AI market frenzy means for them. The rapid stock market ​gains in recent years have been fastest for the top 1%: Between the end of former President Joe Biden’s administration and the second quarter of 2026, midway through Donald Trump’s final term, only ​the top 1% gained a bigger slice of the national wealth pie, according to Federal Reserve data. From the 99th percentile down, the share grew smaller, the data ⁠show. A bigger pie The lower 99% have not been left out entirely, though. Household wealth jumped 16.5% from the end of the Biden administration through mid-2026, rising about $26 trillion in absolute terms. While less than half a ​trillion dollars of that went to the least-wealthy half of households, that still represented about a 10% gain. The dichotomy — a rising share to the richest but rising wealth in general — is one of the confounding aspects of ​the U.S. economy today and has prompted questions among economists over whether the country can grow sustainably if the division of wealth continues to get more skewed. Inflation takes a bite out of spending So far, the answer is ... kind of. Sentiment remains sour, but spending surges on. The amount of money going out the door of U.S. households to buy goods and services continues climbing, and in fact on a dollar basis is rising faster than before the pandemic. Economists looking for evidence of a “K shape” to the ​spending — with an upper leg coasting and a lower leg struggling — have reached mixed conclusions. Spending among wealthier households is strong, to be sure, but research by major banks and places like the Richmond Federal Reserve indicate ​spending at the lower end of the income and wealth distribution is at least holding up. Studies of household credit by the New York Fed have shown little evidence of a credit crisis yet among the less well-off. Yet on ‌an inflation-adjusted ⁠basis, what’s known as “real” spending is growing at about the same rate as it was before the pandemic. A rising gap between nominal and real spending shows what’s lost to inflation. And that offers a clue to why the mood seems to have turned against Trump and Republican congressional candidates just a few weeks ahead of midterm elections. Even as households seem able, so far, to chase the cost of living — whether through earnings, wealth or careful shopping — they have to spend more to just keep pace, a grind that economists have identified as one of the main reasons inflation is so corrosive to public opinion. Inflation flows into everything Trump in the 2024 ​presidential campaign offered a clear yardstick to measure his ​success, promising that he would not only tame ⁠inflation but that prices would actually fall from the start of his new term. Lowering the overall level of prices is a perilous idea: In a growing, competitive economy, the price level typically rises, and it falls only during downturns even as relative prices for individual goods and services shift around in both directions. In the last 20 ​months or so, prices have risen, and the level of inflation rebounded from Trump’s first months. Price pressure has persisted as the shock of import tariffs, ​energy costs associated with the ⁠Iran war and now the AI boom have coursed through the economy. The weight of it all can be seen in general statistics. Hourly wage growth and the consumer price index have been increasing at about the same pace, but some of the marquee prices that are top of mind for shoppers and voters, like gasoline and ground beef, have soared. Growth in average hourly pay is just keeping pace with the increase in consumer prices. Housing affordability is a pain point Prices for day-to-day items are things that people learn to manage. Cut back a little ⁠bit here, skip ​a restaurant trip there, stretch the budget with casseroles. Big-ticket items like homes, however, have a broader influence, and can shape how families ​form and grow, how households build wealth over time, and how people think about whether they are getting ahead or are stuck in place. On housing in particular, the pandemic shock has had a long tail, and so far, things have not gotten better under Trump. In ​fact, with bond yields rising, home mortgage rates have jumped more than a full percentage point in the past year, intensifying what was already an unaffordable situation.

articles.title: In 17 US cities, new homes are now cheaper than old ones
articles.summary: New homes used to be more expensive than existing ones. But that's changing as builders navigate a backlog.
articles.body:
Historically, buying a new-construction home meant paying a premium over older options. But that's starting to reverse as builders deal with rising inventory and an ongoing sales slump.

In some places where building activity has been most aggressive, like the Sun Belt, new homes now sell for less on a price-per-square-foot basis than existing homes, according to Zillow data. In Austin, new construction homes now carry a 19.3% discount to existing homes, while in Raleigh, they're 14.2% cheaper.

Homebuilders have been cutting prices and offering incentives such as closing-cost assistance and mortgage rate buydowns to lure buyers. As of August, builders' months of supply — an industry measure of how long it would take to sell off all inventory at today's sales pace — sits at 8.5. More than six months of supply indicates a market where buyers have the upper hand.

Building has been uneven across the country, and in places where new construction is rare, such as the Northeast and the Midwest, buying a new home still usually comes at a hefty premium over existing options.

Claire Boston is a senior reporter for Yahoo Finance covering housing, mortgages, and home insurance.

articles.title: Gas prices on track to break record for most days above $4 a gallon: Chart of the Day
articles.summary: Gasoline prices are on track to break 2022's record for the longest number of days in any year to stay above $4 per gallon.
articles.body:
Gasoline prices have eased in recent weeks, but the national average is still on track to break the record for the most days above $4 per gallon in a single year.

The national average for regular gasoline stood at $4.35 a gallon on Monday, about $0.04 less than a month ago, but about $1.27 more than a year ago, according to AAA data .

By Wednesday, prices are expected to set the 2022 record for the total number of days in a year spent above $4 per gallon, according to Patrick De Haan, head of petroleum analysis at GasBuddy.

Even though gasoline prices have come off their peak of north of $4.50 in May, they remain at record highs for this time of year, JPMorgan analysts noted last month.

Meanwhile, the national average for diesel stood at $6.25 per gallon on Monday, about $0.10 less than a month ago. Diesel costs directly affect the prices of goods and services, given how heavily it is relied upon for farming, trucking, and deliveries.

Because refineries produce diesel and heating oil from the same supply, approaching winter demand is expected to keep upward pressure on prices.

Gasoline and heating oil futures, which move in lockstep with diesel, show a year-to-date surge of more than 86% and 124%, respectively, according to AlphaSpace data.

Oil prices rose on Monday in the wake of deadly Middle East attacks and amid growing doubts over a Russia-Ukraine "energy ceasefire" announced by President Trump over the weekend.

Brent crude ( BZ=F ) rose to $106 per barrel, while West Texas Intermediate crude ( CL=F ) dropped to $93 a barrel.

Meanwhile, crews were still assessing the aftermath of Hurricane Isaias, which prompted two major refinery shutdowns along the Gulf Coast.

Ines Ferre is a Senior Business Reporter for Yahoo Finance covering the US stock market, publicly traded companies, and commodities.

articles.title: Retail prices of 41 of 42 essential commodities up in a year; onion rates shoot up almost 113%
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Retail prices of 41 of the 42 essential commodities monitored by govt have risen over the past year, with potato being the only exception.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Retail prices of 41 of the 42 essential commodities monitored by govt have risen over the past year, with potato being the only exception. Onion prices have recorded the sharpest increase, surging nearly 113%, followed by sugar (nearly 22%) and sunflower oil (around 18%), according to price monitoring data of the consumer affairs department.Rising food prices have been a key factor behind retail inflation climbing to a nearly two-year high of 5.5% in Sept, according to official data released by the statistics ministry on Monday. Year-on-year food inflation stood at 7.74% in Sept.Official data across different commodity categories show that among pulses, tur dal recorded the sharpest increase in average retail price, rising to around Rs 129 per kg on Monday from Rs 113 a year ago. Prices were higher in the four metros, ranging from Rs 140 to Rs 145 per kg. The average price of chana dal rose 6.4% to Rs 91 per kg on Monday from Rs 85 a year ago. Govt is likely to consider releasing chana from its buffer stock soon, sources said.Among edible oils, sunflower oil recorded the steepest increase in average retail price, reaching Rs 191 per litre, nearly 18% higher than a year ago. It was followed by palm oil, which rose 15.2%, and soya oil, up 14.6%. Mustard oil prices also increased to Rs 204 per litre from Rs 188 a year ago.Data also show that the average price of regular rice has risen nearly 12% to Rs 47 per kg, while increases in wheat and atta (wheat flour) prices have been marginal. Sugar prices, though moderating to Rs 56 per kg on Monday from nearly Rs 59 a month ago, remain almost 22% higher than a year ago. The increase has been attributed to lower-than-expected production.Among major vegetables, onion prices remain elevated at Rs 53 per kg, while potato prices have fallen by over 6%. Tomato was selling at Rs 42 per kg on Monday, compared with Rs 36 a year ago.Trade sources attributed the rise in onion prices to estimates of a 5-7% decline in kharif onion production in Maharashtra, the country’s largest onion-producing state, due to a reduction in acreage and delayed monsoon rains. articles.title: He gave up his land for road widening and got TDRs which he sold for Rs 6.02 crore to a builder; landowner gets tax notice, ITAT rules proceeds taxable as capital gains but allows land cost deduction
articles.summary: You get Transferable Development Rights from the government by giving up a part of your land and sell them to a builder.
articles.body: You get Transferable Development Rights from the government by giving up a part of your land and sell them to a builder. Are you liable to pay capital gains tax?In one such case a landowner received Transferable Development Rights (TDRs) but assumed them to be capital receipts. The Income Tax Department sent him a notice.What the case is aboutWhen the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP) approached the landowner to acquire a portion of his property for road widening, he agreed to surrender the land. In return, he received TDRs, which are certificates that are issued to landowners when the government takes over privately owned land for public purposes.Also Read | Rs 5.2 crore cash deposit, but Rs 7.65 lakh shown in ITR: Grain trader wins tax case after ITAT quashes notice, finds bank account was disclosed in Form 3CDThese rights can be used to construct additional floors on another property or sold to builders who want to undertake development projects, according to an ET report.The landowner chose to sell the TDRs he had received for surrendering 2,839 square metres of land. He sold them to a builder for Rs 6 crore but did not pay income tax on the proceeds. His understanding was that the amount received from the sale was a capital receipt and was therefore not taxable.The Income Tax Department, however, took a different view. The Deputy Commissioner of Income Tax in Koramangala, Bengaluru, sought to bring the entire Rs 6 crore within the tax net and levy capital gains tax on the amount.Disputing the department's position, the landowner challenged the decision before the National Faceless Appeal Centre (NFAC) in Delhi. The NFAC dismissed his appeal on July 8, 2025, prompting him to approach the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT), Bangalore.Also Read | Builder promised to pay stamp duty on Rs 1.6 crore plot, later called it a typo; MahaRERA orders him to pay charges plus interest for delayed possession to buyerWhy did the landowner lose the case?The tribunal delivered its ruling on August 14, 2026. While the landowner secured some relief, he largely lost the case, with the ITAT Bangalore holding that the sale of TDRs was taxable as capital gains.It directed the Assessing Officer (AO) to allow him credit for the cost attributable to the land surrendered in exchange for the development rights.Chartered Accountant Suresh Surana told ET: “The ITAT Bangalore rejected the landowner’s assumption that he doesn’t need to pay tax on TDRs, as they have no ascertainable cost of acquisition and thus are essentially a capital receipt not liable for tax.”The tribunal did not accept this argument. It held that TDRs qualified as capital assets and that the proceeds from their sale were subject to capital gains tax.To support his contention that TDRs should not be taxed, the landowner had cited the Supreme Court's judgment in B.C. Srinivasa Setty and the Bombay High Court's ruling in Sambhaji Nagar Co-operative Housing Society Ltd.However, the ITAT Bangalore distinguished these judgments on the basis of the facts involved. It explained that cases such as Sambhaji Nagar concerned self-generated development rights.Also Read | Delhi couple repaid Rs 1.41 crore home loan, but the bank lost their original sale deed property papers; consumer commission orders Rs 15 lakh compensation plus Rs 50,000 costsIn those cases, taxpayers gained additional development potential because of changes in development regulations, without surrendering a separately identifiable asset in return.The tribunal found that the landowner’s case was different in a material respect. He had given up an identifiable and valuable asset, namely his land and building, to obtain the TDRs.On this basis, the ITAT Bangalore treated the transaction as having two distinct stages. In the first, the landowner surrendered his land to BBMP and received TDRs in exchange. In the second, he sold those development rights for cash.The ITAT Bangalore held that Section 2(47), which includes an exchange within the definition of a transfer, applied to the transaction.The TDRs received by the landowner were therefore capital assets acquired in exchange for the land he surrendered. The tribunal concluded that he had paid for the TDRs through the surrender of his property.Surana said: “Consequently, the capital gains computation mechanism did not fail, and the Rs. 6.02 crore received on their subsequent sale could not be treated as an exempt capital receipt.”The landowner also pointed out that his brother had received consideration for similar TDRs and that the Income Tax Department had accepted the amount as exempt while assessing his brother's income.Also Read | He moved to Canada and rented his Punjab house for Rs 20,000 a month, then sought eviction to use it during India visits; Punjab & Haryana HC rules against landlord, allows tenant to stayHowever, the ITAT Bangalore did not consider the treatment given to his brother's case sufficient grounds to grant the landowner the same tax exemption. As Surana explained, the tribunal observed that an assessment order concerning another taxpayer does not permanently bind the Income Tax Department. This is particularly relevant where a claim may have been accepted without adequately examining the applicable facts and legal provisions.While the ITAT Bangalore rejected the landowner’s argument that the TDR sale was not taxable, it did not accept the Income Tax Department's position on the cost of acquisition without further consideration.Since the landowner had received the TDRs in return for surrendering 2,839 square metres of land, the cost attributable to that land had to be taken into account while calculating his capital gains.The tribunal found that the AO had failed to provide for the cost associated with the 2,839 square metres surrendered to BBMP.The ruling means Talera is liable to pay tax on the capital gains arising from the transaction, but this does not automatically make the entire Rs 6.02 crore sale proceeds taxable. The AO must first calculate the appropriate cost attributable to the surrendered land and account for that amount, along with any other deductions permitted under Section 48, before determining the taxable capital gain.Also Read | Man had Rs 2 crore bank deposit and didn’t file ITR, faced Rs 2.51 crore tax addition; ITAT Chennai quashes reassessment after Income Tax Department missed 6-year deadline by 5 daysYou use AI every day. articles.title: Dow rises, S&P 500 near record as Wall Street braces for key US data
articles.summary: Wall Street stocks traded mixed on Monday, with the S&P 500 holding near its record high as gains in energy shares offset losses in technology stocks.
articles.body: Wall Street stocks traded mixed on Monday, with the S&P 500 holding near its record high as gains in energy shares offset losses in technology stocks. Investors also turned their attention to a fresh round of corporate earnings and key US inflation data due later this week.The S&P 500 rose 0.1%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 0.4%, adding 228 points. The Nasdaq Composite slipped 0.2%, reflecting pressure on some of the technology stocks that have helped drive the market's gains this year.Energy shares advanced as crude oil prices climbed amid concerns over global supplies. Brent crude, the international benchmark, rose 2% to $106.77 per barrel. Oil prices have fluctuated sharply in recent weeks amid uncertainty surrounding the US war with Iran and its implications for energy supplies and inflation. Chevron gained 1.4%.Technology stocks were among the biggest drags on the market, with Micron Technology falling 2.8% and Advanced Micro Devices declining 2.4%. Investors are looking for evidence that the surge in artificial intelligence-related investment will translate into sustained earnings growth and justify the sector's strong stock-market performance.Artificial intelligence continues to support the outlook for technology companies and their suppliers, but questions remain over the longer-term returns from the technology. As companies begin reporting quarterly results, investors will be watching whether earnings can sustain the momentum behind market valuations.Oil prices remain another key variable for markets. Rising crude costs can push up petrol and diesel prices, increase transportation expenses and feed into the cost of goods. This could complicate the Federal Reserve's efforts to bring inflation down to its 2% target.Investors will get fresh readings on price pressures and consumer demand this week. The US consumer price index (CPI), due on Wednesday, is expected to show annual inflation rising to 3.6% in September from 3.4% in August. Producer price inflation and retail sales data are scheduled for Thursday, offering further insight into business costs and household spending.The data could influence expectations for the Federal Reserve's interest-rate decisions. Persistent inflation has kept the prospect of further rate increases in focus, while higher bond yields have raised borrowing costs across the economy. The 10-year US Treasury yield recently touched its highest level since 2002 before easing to 5.24% late Friday. US bond markets were closed on Monday for the Columbus Day holiday.The housing market will also be in focus, as elevated mortgage rates weigh on affordability and demand. Investors are due to receive an update on home sales on Tuesday.Meanwhile, the latest earnings season gathers pace with results from major US banks. Citigroup, JPMorgan Chase and Wells Fargo are scheduled to report on Tuesday, followed by Bank of America on Wednesday. Their results are expected to provide clues about lending activity, consumer finances and the broader economic outlook.Elsewhere, European markets advanced, while most Asian markets ended lower. articles.title: Sandisk stock is this bull market's emergent star
articles.summary: Sandisk stock (SNDK) has soared over 3,000% since its IPO a year and a half ago.
articles.body:
Sandisk stock ( SNDK ) has soared over 3,000% since its IPO a year and a half ago.

As Yahoo Finance's Julie Hyman pointed out on this fourth anniversary of the bull market , Sandisk has had the best performance of any S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) stock, outrunning Palantir (No. 2, up 2,490%), Vertiv (No. 3, up 2,125%), Nvidia (No. 4, up 1,894%), and Micron (No. 5, up 1,851%).

There's one caveat to that title: Sandisk's incredible run is purely a 2025-2026 story. In February 2025, Western Digital ( WDC ) spun off its flash memory unit, and Sandisk began trading as its own entity at $52 per share, according to Yahoo Finance data.

As of 2 p.m. ET, shares of Sandisk are trading at $1,479, and the company boasts a market cap of over $200 billion. (Sandisk and other chip names are falling on Monday after a memory innovation from a Chinese company.)

Following Sandisk's listing, the company benefited from surging demand for NAND data storage technology, driven by the AI data center build-out and companies training generative AI models.

In recent quarters, Sandisk's data center business has accounted for a quarter to a third of its overall revenue as the AI memory supply bottleneck has given memory makers like Sandisk enormous pricing power.

At the company's investor day in August, Sandisk's management shared a bullish outlook for annual revenue growth in the mid-to-high teens between 2028 and 2030. The company also forecast non-GAAP gross margins at about 80%.

Even among other memory stocks, like Micron ( MU ), Sandisk emerges as a highflier, though Micron's comparable 979% gain since Sandisk's IPO date is nothing to sneeze at. Micron produces DRAM and high-bandwidth memory, as well as NAND.

The overwhelming takeaway from this bull market is that the AI build-out is minting the next wave of stock winners.

From Nvidia, which designs the chips and hardware that go into data centers, to Palantir, which produces the software that runs the application layer, to Vertiv, which creates the technology to regulate data centers' power and temperatures, artificial intelligence has powered this bull market — which coincided with the release of OpenAI's ( OPAI.PVT ) ChatGPT.

articles.title: HCLTech Q2 YoY revenue up 2.2% to $3.7 billion, narrows FY27 guidance
articles.summary: HCLTech Q2 dollar revenue rises 2.2% YoY to $3.7B; EBIT margin 18.2%. FY27 constant-currency guidance narrowed to 2.5%-4%; AI revenue hits $219M.
articles.body: Mumbai: HCLTech’s dollar revenue rose to $3.7 billion in the September quarter, up 2% sequentially and 2.2% year on year. In constant currency terms, revenue grew 2.3% sequentially and 2.6% year on year. EBIT margin expanded 131 basis points sequentially and 71 basis points year on year to 18.2%.The company’s services business grew 3% sequentially, generating more than $100 million in incremental revenue. About $50 million came from advanced AI and the remaining $50 million from the core business, where HCLTech is gaining market share through AI-driven services.HCLTech narrowed its FY27 company revenue growth guidance to 2.5%-4% in constant currency terms from the 1%-4% announced in Q1. Services revenue growth guidance was revised to 3%-4% from the earlier range of 1.5%-4.5%.CEO C Vijayakumar said the company retained the midpoint of both guidance ranges despite narrowing them, reflecting caution about extrapolating recent improvements in demand amid a volatile business environment.“Although we saw demand improve towards the end of the first quarter, we remained cautious because the business environment has been volatile over the past two years. We did not want to extrapolate recent positive developments too aggressively,” Vijayakumar said.He said client conversations had been encouraging, with enterprises focused on scaling AI adoption and delivering measurable business outcomes. Clients were also seeking ways to extend AI-driven productivity gains across software development and IT operations, where benefits demonstrated in smaller projects had proved harder to replicate across entire organisations.Vijayakumar said it was too early to call an industry-wide inflection point, though HCLTech expected FY27 to be better than the current year. The company will review its guidance after the third quarter. Its data centre investments are expected to contribute meaningfully from the second half of FY28, given the long gestation period of such projects.Advanced AI revenue, which includes AI factories, physical AI, agentic AI and AI advisory services, reached $219 million in the quarter, equivalent to an annualised run rate of about $876 million. It grew 28.4% sequentially and 78% year on year in constant currency terms.“Advanced AI should deliver higher margins than our existing business,” Vijayakumar said, adding that the company would reinvest gains to strengthen its AI capabilities and gain market share.CFO Shiv Walia said HCLTech retained its EBIT margin guidance of 17.5%-18.5% despite acquisition-related costs. “Despite these costs, we retained the margin range by absorbing the impact,” he said, referring to amortisation and transition services costs.HCLTech’s global workforce stood at about 2.3 lakh at the end of the Sept quarter, after increasing by 6,450 employees during the period. This represented quarterly growth of 2.9% and annualised headcount growth of 1.6%.The company added 6,136 freshers during the quarter, about 1,000 more than in the year-ago period. Around 15% were in its elite engineer category. HCLTech expects to hire about 10,000 freshers for the full year.On the US govt’s suspension of permanent labour certification processing, HCLTech CHRO Ramachandran Sundararajan said: “The number of PERM applications we have filed over the past couple of years has been very small. articles.title: PERM certifications at 13 IT companies fell to 607 in nine months from 1,670 in FY25
articles.summary: PERM certifications at 13 IT services firms dropped to 607 in 9M FY26 from 1,670 in FY25, as the US suspended PERM processing for major players.
articles.body: Bengaluru: IT firms had shrugged off concerns over their dependence on the US green-card route well before the US administration announced the suspension of PERM processing, with certified applications already declining sharply. Thirteen major IT services companies recorded 607 certified permanent labour certification (PERM) applications in the first nine months of FY26, compared with 1,670 in FY25 and 1,756 in FY24, according to Kotak Institutional Equities.Kotak has reported certified PERM applications across major IT services companies with September fiscal year-ends.The decline comes as the US administration has suspended new and pending PERM applications involving TCS, Infosys, HCL Technologies, Wipro, Cognizant and Capgemini. PERM is a key labour-certification stage in the process of obtaining employment-based green cards.TCS recorded just two certifications in the first nine months of FY26, against 505 in FY25 and 597 in FY24. Wipro also had two certifications, compared with 206 in FY25. HCLTech recorded 28, down from 94 in FY25 and six in FY24.Infosys had 12 certified applications in FY25, while the report shows no figure for the first nine months of FY26 or FY24. Cognizant recorded 741 certifications in FY24, but the report does not provide figures for FY25 or the first nine months of FY26. Capgemini had seven certifications in the first nine months of FY26, against 290 in FY25 and 50 in FY24.Among the other companies covered, LTM recorded 168 certifications in the first nine months of FY26, up from 127 in FY25 and 159 in FY24. Persistent Systems reported 58, compared with 16 in FY25 and 10 in FY24. Mphasis recorded 82 certifications in the first nine months of FY26, against 132 in FY25 and 79 in FY24, while Hexaware Technologies had 73, compared with 24 and one, respectively.Accenture recorded 182 certifications in the first nine months of FY26, against 226 in FY25 and 71 in FY24. Coforge had five certifications in the first nine months of FY26, compared with 23 in FY25, while Tech Mahindra had no figure reported for the period, against 15 in FY25 and 42 in FY24.TCS CEO K Krithivasan told TOI that green cards have never been a key part of the company’s workforce strategy. TCS has significantly reduced permanent residency applications for H-1B employees and stepped up local hiring in the US. Infosys and HCLTech said the PERM suspension was unlikely to have a material impact on their operations.Kotak’s report said the suspension was unlikely to have a meaningful impact on delivery or earnings because Indian IT companies have increasingly localised their US workforces, reducing their dependence on visa-based staffing. Employees with pending PERM applications represent a smaller subset of the remaining visa-dependent workforce, it said.The brokerage said increased reliance on subcontractors could raise near-term costs, but greater offshoring should provide an offset over time.You use AI every day. articles.summary: Zetwerk plans Rs 2,830 crore IPO fresh issue; order book Rs 12,500 crore incl. Rs 2,000 crore US transformers, driven by AI-led data centre demand.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Manufacturing marketplace Zetwerk, which is preparing for an IPO, has an order book of around Rs 12,500 crore, including transformer orders worth about Rs 2,000 crore, largely for the US market. The growth is being driven by the artificial intelligence boom, which is fuelling data centre expansion and extending delivery timelines for critical power equipment, co-founder and CEO Amrit Acharya told TOI.Acharya rejected earlier reports that Zetwerk had sought a $4 billion valuation. He said the company raised about Rs 500 crore in March at a post-money valuation of Rs 27,000 crore, broadly in line with its IPO pricing.Zetwerk’s IPO comprises a fresh issue of up to Rs 2,830 crore and an offer for sale by existing shareholders. articles.title: Cuba forges ahead with renewable energy plans amid US oil blockade
articles.summary: Cuban energy minister denies link to fuel shipments intercepted by US, says oil imports by private firms insufficient.
articles.body:
The Cuban government is pushing ahead with its plans to transition to renewable energy, amid a de facto oil blockade from the United States that has strangled the island’s economy.

In an interview with the Reuters news agency on Monday, Cuban Minister of Energy and Mines Vicente de la O Levy explained that the blockade has forced Cuba to explore domestic alternatives to foreign fuel imports.

“We are seeking our own alternative solutions, using our own resources, our sun, wind, tides, fuel, Cuban crude oil and the gas produced in our wells,” de la O Levy said.

He said 144 solar farms with a combined capacity of about 1,418 megawatts have been installed on the island in recent years.

China has been the largest supplier of solar panels to the island, and shipments have increased since the blockade began in early January.

At the time, US President Donald Trump halted all oil shipments from Venezuela, a close ally of the Cuban government.

Later that month, Trump also announced he would impose heavy tariffs on any country that exported oil to Cuba, justifying the threat by calling the island’s government a “national security” threat.

Since then, only a single oil tanker from Russia has reached Havana. The US has increased its shipments of oil to Cuba’s private sector, but it has largely barred fuel exports for nationalised industries on the communist-led island.

The government-run electrical grid, widely considered to be antiquated, relies heavily on fossil fuels. Only 40 percent of Cuba’s electricity comes from ‌‌‌‌domestic ‌‌‌‌oil production, according to the International Energy Agency.

As of 2023, only nine percent of the country’s energy consumption was covered by renewable sources.

De la O Levy admitted in his interview with Reuters that the country was facing difficulties. The blockade has caused shortages of medicine, water and fuel, pushing Cuba to the brink of a humanitarian crisis.

“We are surviving and moving forward, little by little, even if not at the pace we would like,” he said.

“We face long hours of blackouts and lack fuel for cooking and transportation. We lack fuel, but we are gradually making headway through our own solutions and our people.”

Cuba’s production of domestic crude oil remains stable, he added, but is almost entirely allocated to power plants.

The United Nations and human rights watchdogs have criticised the oil blockade as a violation of international law.

Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodriguez Parrilla also condemned the oil blockade in his speech at the UN General Assembly last month.

“It is an unusual and unprecedented action,” Rodriguez said of the blockade.

“A superpower unilaterally deprives all states of their right to export the commodities that they wish to the country that they wish.”

The US has maintained an economic embargo on Cuba for more than 60 years, since the Cold War era.

But since taking office for a second term as president, Trump has sought to squeeze Cuba’s economy further, as part of a “maximum pressure” campaign. His administration has indicated that it wants to topple Cuba’s government .

On October 7, US authorities announced they had seized 90 biodiesel fuel shipments valued at over $2.8m destined for Cuba.

“These shipments were part of an attempt to unlawfully export fuel to Cuba in violation of federal export laws,” US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) said in a statement.

But in his interview with Reuters, de la O Levy denied the Cuban government had any link to the shipments.

“No Cuban state-owned company has managed to secure a fuel contract, whether for small or large quantities,” he said.

He added that any US oil shipments to private firms fall far short of the country’s requirements.

“I would venture to say that the amount entering the country doesn’t even cover 3 percent of its fuel needs,” de la O Levy said.

articles.title: Energy prices rise after Trump’s ‘energy ceasefire’ fails to move Russia or Ukraine
articles.summary: Oil and gas prices rose Monday after an “energy ceasefire” announced by President Donald Trump on Sunday failed to gain traction.
articles.body: Oil and gas prices rose Monday after an “energy ceasefire” announced by President Donald Trump on Sunday failed to gain traction. Brent crude oil jumped 2% to almost $108 per barrel and U.S. crude oil rose more than 2% to about $94. Meanwhile, diesel futures fully erased a small drop they saw last week. Just weeks out from the Nov. 3 midterm elections, the price pressures are mounting. Republicans face a steep climb to maintain their majorities in Congress, and voters across the country cite high gas prices as a key issue affecting their votes. The average nationwide price of diesel fuel Monday was $6.26 per gallon, nearly 80% higher than it had been at the start of the year, according to AAA data. The rising prices Monday came less than 24 hours after Trump declared that a ceasefire had been agreed to. “Effective immediately, there is an ENERGY CEASEFIRE in the War between Russia and Ukraine. Both parties have agreed. Do not break it!” Trump wrote on Truth Social. Shortly after the president’s post, Russia renewed strikes against Ukrainian energy assets. Pressed by reporters Monday as to why neither the Kremlin nor Kyiv had firmly committed to his ceasefire, Trump indicated that he knew when he made the announcement on Sunday that he did not yet have a commitment from either side. “They agreed, you know why? Because I said ‘You agree,” Trump told reporters at the White House. As for getting Russian President Vladimir Putin to commit, Trump said, “We’re going to see what happens.” Asked if he was aware that Russia had already violated the ceasefire Trump had announced, the president replied, “I’m not sure about that,” before claiming there had been “violations on both sides.” Ceasefire déjà vu President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine learned about Trump’s ceasefire from media reports and was given no advance warning. He reiterated his position that Ukraine was open to an agreement not to target enemy energy infrastructure as long as Moscow agrees to it, too. In the meantime, Russia continued with “glide bomb strikes and strikes on our energy infrastructure,” Zelenskyy said Monday, noting that a power plant in Kharkiv had recently been attacked. “Ukraine has proposed many de-escalatory steps. Putin had one answer to all of them — ‘nyet,’” Zelenskyy said, using the Russian word for “no.” The Kremlin on Monday neither confirmed nor denied having agreed to a deal. Trump’s Sunday announcement closely mirrored a similar post he made in September, when he announced that “Ukraine has agreed not to hit Russian Energy targets. Russia has agreed to do, likewise!” There, too, Zelenskyy said Ukraine’s participation hinged on Russia’s agreement to comply, which never came. Neither Ukrainian nor Russian strikes on the other’s energy assets slowed down in September. Trump’s deal with Putin The dubious ceasefire Trump declared over the weekend followed a stunning announcement Friday in which the president said Russia would supply millions of barrels of diesel “to the American and Global Marketplace.” The announcement came after a phone call Friday between Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin that reportedly lasted over an hour. Trump said the deal with Putin would “immediately supply over 300,000 Tons of Diesel Fuel to the American and Global Marketplace.” That would translate into about 2.25 million barrels of diesel, or less diesel than the United States uses in just one day. Further details and logistics of Russia’s plan had yet to be announced Monday. In addition to the Russia deal, Trump has pressured G7 allies to release more diesel fuel supplies in recent days and lifted domestic restrictions on an off-road variety of diesel. In order to clear a legal path for the diesel deal, the Treasury Department announced a six-month suspension of the fuel sanctions imposed on the Kremlin in 2022 for its illegal invasion of Ukraine. Ukrainian officials, European allies and some U.S. lawmakers were aghast at the deal and the U.S. decision to unilaterally ease Russia sanctions. Trump defended the deal Monday, calling it “the right choice for the American People.” Trump also said more diesel fuel would be made available “within a short period of time,” if Russia’s refineries could produce it. Questions about Russia’s capacity Yet experts are highly skeptical that there will be any significant resumption of Russian diesel exports in the near term. Due to Ukrainian strikes deep inside Russia, refiners that produce oil, gas and diesel have suffered heavy damage. “Reported gasoline output is down by 20% compared with 2025 levels, while diesel production is estimated to have fallen by nearly 30%, prompting the government to restrict fuel exports to protect domestic supplies,” analysts at the International Energy Agency wrote in a September report. For weeks, Trump has focused on the price of diesel fuel, which began rising as a result of the Iran war that the U.S. and Israel launched in February. In July, escalations in the Russia-Ukraine war began adding to the pressure on diesel prices. As Ukrainian drones systematically targeted Russian energy assets, the Kremlin responded by restricting diesel exports in order to preserve its supply for domestic use. Until then, Russia had been one of the world’s top exporters of refined oil products, which include diesel fuel. Russia said Friday that it would lift some of its export restrictions in order to accommodate the deal with Trump. But it was unclear how fast that would happen.

articles.title: Intel aims to boost AI turnaround with new GPU chips to take on Nvidia
articles.summary: Intel is diving further into the AI GPU market.
articles.body:
Intel's ( INTC ) turnaround effort is getting a strong boost from the global AI build-out, which is driving increased demand for its central processing units (CPUs) .

But the company is also expanding further into the graphics processing unit (GPU) market with the debut of its Intel GPU D-Series processors . Formerly codenamed Crescent Island, the D-Series chips are designed for AI inferencing, running AI models and services.

Rather than individual chips that slot into server blades like Nvidia's ( NVDA ) Blackwell processors, Intel's D-Series GPUs are deployed via PCIe cards, similar in appearance to the graphics cards gamers install in desktop computers.

Intel said it's working with a number of OEMs, ODMs, neoclouds, and others to roll out D-Series systems, including ASUS ( 2357.TW ), HPE ( HPE ), Dell ( DELL ), Supermicro, and others.

Intel has been working to gain a greater foothold in the GPU market, ranging from consumer products to the data center, including its Gaudi AI accelerator and GPU Flex Series cards.

Intel stock is up 183% year to date and roughly 175% over the past 12 months, largely driven by interest in its CPUs.

The processors, which fell out of favor in the early days of the generative AI explosion, have become increasingly important for AI providers and data center builders with the advent of AI agents.

That's because while GPUs and AI accelerators power the AI models and agents that rely on them, the tasks agents perform, such as sorting through databases, launching apps, loading websites, and more, run on CPUs.

But Intel is facing increasing competition in the CPU data center race from longtime rival AMD ( AMD ), which is rapidly growing its share of data center revenue in the space.

Arm-based ( ARM ) CPUs are also gaining a greater foothold in the data center, thanks to Nvidia's decision to launch standalone CPU racks running its Grace chip .

Qualcomm ( QCOM ) has also entered the fight with its own Arm-based CPUs , AI accelerators, memory products, and networking capabilities as it seeks to diversify beyond its reliance on the smartphone market.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: Retail inflation based on the consumer price index (CPI) rose to a nine-month high of 5.5% in Sept (y-o-y) from 4.8% in Aug, on account of a surge in food prices, which strained household costs, National Statistics Office data released Monday showed. This was the first time that retail inflation crossed the 5% mark under the new CPI series, which was released earlier this year, remaining above the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) 4% target for the fourth consecutive month, although the headline figure still remains within the central bank's tolerance band of 2-6%.Data came days after RBI raised repo rates by 25 basis points amid the price pressure. Food inflation was estimated at 7.7% in Sept, compared with 6% in Aug. With 108% increase, onions recorded the steepest price rise in Sept, compared with 49% in Aug. Garlic prices accelerated 55% from 44%, while lemon prices surged 36% during the month. Some vegetables, however, continued to provide relief, with the prices of potato (-11%), tomato (-8%) and lady finger (-4.5%) falling in Sept.The impact of the prolonged conflict in West Asia is also showing up, with sectors such as transport and restaurants seeing steady increase in costs. Goods transport services saw 14.7% inflation, while restaurant services saw 9.4% inflation - driven by higher fuel costs.Rural inflation (6.1%) tended to be higher given the higher weight of food items in the basket, as compared to the urban areas (4.9%). The southern states of Andhra Pradesh (6.3%), Karnataka (5.9%), Tamil Nadu (6.8%) and Odisha (6.7%) had higher inflation relative to others.Bank of Baroda chief economist Madan Sabnavis said transmission of higher wholesale price index (WPI) into CPI is yet to be seen, with industries such as durables, FMCG, automobile having announced an increase in prices. It will reflect in the coming months. "The challenge will be the third quarter where inflation will peak at around 6%. articles.title: Bumble's potential $1 billion sale marks an embarrassing fall from the dating app's peak
articles.summary: Bumble stock rose 52% on Monday following a Wall Street Journal report that it would be taken private for $1 billion. The company will go down as a great cas...
articles.body:
Bumble ( BMBL ) spent several years unable to find the right match with investors. It will go down as a great case study in what happens when a digital company has no moat, frequent management changes, and faces rapid technological change.

Bumble stock rose 52% on Monday following a Wall Street Journal report that it would be taken private for $1 billion. The purchase price is light years away from Bumble's peak valuation around the time of its 2021 IPO of $14 billion.

A Bumble spokesperson didn't return Yahoo Finance's request for comment.

The reported buyer is Ithaca Holdings, a recently founded investment firm.

The reported $1 billion purchase — well in excess of its $335 million market cap prior to the news — seems exorbitant for two reasons.

First, the company's financial performance has been horrible, owing to fierce competition. It also doesn't help that millions are now forming relationships with personal AI agents rather than interacting with potential human companions.

Second quarter sales crashed 15.2%, led by a steep drop in the Bumble app. The number of paying users tanked. Adjusted operating profits plunged to $72.9 million from $94.6 million a year ago.

This happened despite founder Whitney Wolfe Herd returning as CEO in January 2025, replacing high-profile hire and former Slack CEO Lidiane Jones, who made significant changes to the organization.

Wolfe Herd has sought to stabilize the business, to no avail. The latest attempt to jump-start growth was to officially end Bumble's "women first" messaging rule. Any person in a match can now send the initial message.

The second factor in play is a revitalized Match ( MTCH ) under newish CEO Spencer Rascoff.

Rascoff has pushed the company into live events for people to meet, with more on the way.

He has also improved Tinder's user experience to focus more on quality engagement, bringing the company to the cusp of delivering daily active user growth after many quarters of decline.

Match Group reported mixed second quarter financial results, with sales up 1% from the prior year.

Despite top-line friction from user declines at Tinder, the company's bottom-line performance proved more resilient. Match posted a 14% rise in adjusted operating profits.

The continued subscriber pressure at Tinder outweighed the strong 22% growth of its Hinge brand.

"I think just as social media made people's connection with one another worse," Rascoff told Yahoo Finance in a September interview. "I mean, it's called social media, but it's not even really that social anymore. It's not about connecting with your friends. It's more about consuming content of creators."
